content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.0+), especially in early 30d forecasts.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (especially -1.5 to -0.7), particularly after recent highs.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings, leading to overshoots in 30d forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts often stay too high after 3-5 consecutive price peaks, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment was negative 3-5 days prior, model often fails to adjust downward in 30d forecast.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts consistently overestimate early periods (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimate later periods (last 10-15 days) when sentiment turns negative.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3-5 days; sentiment decay should be modeled with exponential decay or smoothing.
